status_summary: Two of the three parts the Foreword paragraph restates are operative: DEI offices and training were ordered abolished on 2025-01-27 and GAO later counted all 41 remaining DEI positions as abolished or restructured (see c04-03), and the transgender service policy has been enforced since the Supreme Court stayed the Shilling injunction on 2025-05-06, while the D.C. Circuit on 2026-06-01 left the Talbott injunction in place for the named currently serving plaintiffs and the government petitioned for certiorari on 2026-08-27 (see c04-01). The China priority is only partly aligned: the 2026 National Defense Strategy ranks China second to homeland defense (see c04-08). No record tracks the sole-mission framing as such, so the stage is derived from the three detailed records.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14183, Prioritizing Military Excellence and Readiness, signed (published 2025-02-03 at 90 FR 8757): states that gender dysphoria does not meet military medical standards, directs revision of the Defense medical standards instructions and bars accommodation of gender identities that differ from sex.

Executive Order 14185, Restoring America's Fighting Force, signed (published 2025-02-03 at 90 FR 8763): directs the abolition of DOD diversity, equity and inclusion offices and bars listed concepts in DOD education.
Secretary of Defense memo ends race- and sex-based goals and DEI working groups and bars teaching of critical race theory, DEI and gender ideology, per press reports (memo PDF not opened).
GAO reports DOD abolished or restructured all 41 remaining civilian and military positions with primary DEI duties.

Supreme Court grants the government's application in United States v. Shilling and stays the 2025-03-27 preliminary injunction of the W.D. Washington against the transgender service policy, pending appeal and any certiorari petition.
timeline.source: Supreme Court of the United States

timeline.event: The FY2026 NDAA becomes Public Law 119-60 (date shown on govinfo.gov); its sections 1249 and 1268 provide for oversight of U.S. military posture in Europe and on the Korean Peninsula.
The Department releases the 2026 National Defense Strategy, which ranks homeland defense first and deterring China in the Indo-Pacific second.

The D.C. Circuit (Wilkins, Walker and Rogers, JJ.; No. 25-5087; argued 2026-01-22) affirms the Talbott preliminary injunction in part and vacates it in part: it stands for the named plaintiffs who are currently serving, is vacated for named plaintiffs seeking to enlist, and is narrowed to the named plaintiffs. Judge Wilkins announces the judgment, Judge Rogers concurs in part and dissents in part, and Judge Walker dissents; press reports describe the decision as 2-1.
timeline.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit (opinion, No. 25-5087)

timeline.event: The Solicitor General files a petition for a writ of certiorari in United States v. Talbott (No. 26-272) seeking review of the D.C. Circuit's 2026-06-01 decision; the case is docketed 2026-09-01. Respondents' time to respond is extended to 2026-11-02 (order of 2026-09-25), and amicus briefs supporting the government were filed 2026-10-01. The docket shows no ruling. Stars and Stripes reports that a two-week trial is set for January 2027.
timeline.source: Supreme Court of the United States (docket No. 26-272)

timeline.event: Department of War release announces a directive halting new tenured civilian faculty appointments at the service academies (release undated on the page; date per the Secretary of War memo as recorded in c04-03).

title: End social experimentation in the military; make warfighting and China the priority
uncertainties: Stage derivation: c04-03 is implemented 72, c04-01 is implemented 70 and c04-08 is in_progress 45. Because the Foreword sentence bundles all three and the China element sits below the others (the 2026 strategy ranks homeland defense above China, which differs from the Mandate's order), the combined stage is in_progress 55, inside the band. Implemented 65 is defensible if the sole-mission wording is read mainly as the DEI and transgender items. The sole-mission statement is broad and no separate measure of it was found; this record does not assess other military policies. The 2026 court events were copied from c04-01, which cites the D.C. Circuit opinion and the Supreme Court docket for No. 26-272. The source for the Secretary of War directive is undated on its page. The court status follows c04-01 (pending certiorari petition); the policy operates during the appeals except as to the named Talbott plaintiffs.
